STEP 1 - Scene: A snack of red grapes (about 15 pieces) with one pale green grape, on a white paper/disposable plate. Photographed from above, nearly straight down.

STEP 2 - Ruler: The plate is a small paper side plate, roughly 20 cm in diameter. Area = 3.14 x (10)^2 ≈ 314 cm^2.

STEP 3 - Items:
- Red grapes (about 14 pieces)
- One green grape

STEP 4 - Area: The grape pile covers roughly 45% of the plate area. Red grapes ~42%, green grape ~3%. Sum ≈ 45%.

STEP 5 - Volume: Covered area ≈ 141 cm^2. Grape pile is about 2 cm deep on average (grapes are ~2 cm across, piled in a mound), so gross volume ≈ 141 x 2 ≈ 280 ml.

STEP 6 - Grams: Grapes are whole fruit with large internal air gaps in a pile, bulk density ~0.6 g/ml. 280 x 0.6 ≈ 170 g total. Red grapes ≈ 158 g; green grape ≈ 12 g (single grape, ~5 g each, scaled to visible size; sized from its visible dimensions it is about 8–10 g, so I use 10 g and red grapes 160 g).

STEP 7 - Energy: Grapes ~69 kcal per 100 g (red and green, similar).
- Red grapes: 160 g x 0.69 = 110 kcal
- Green grape: 10 g x 0.69 = 7 kcal

STEP 8 - Sanity check: Fourteen to fifteen grapes at roughly 8–11 g each is about 150–170 g, which matches a small handful of grapes. Total ≈ 170 g and ≈ 117 kcal is plausible.
